intended_object: The canonical linear isomorphism E/p ≅ q when q is a complement of p in the module E: a class [x] goes to the projection of x onto q along p, and y ∈ q goes back to [y]. Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation:
The forward map lifts `q.projectionOnto p h.symm`, the projection onto q along p, through the quotient by p. This is well defined because the projection kills p, which is the `by simp` side condition. The backward map is `mkQ ∘ q.subtype`. The two proof obligations check that the maps are mutually inverse: projecting an element y of q gives y back, and x minus its projection lies in p. This is exactly the standard isomorphism, and it matches the docstring.

On generality: Mathlib's quotient module `E ⧸ p` needs `Ring R` and `AddCommGroup E`, so this is the natural setting for the construction. Ring and module are otherwise arbitrary, and there is no finite-dimensionality or other extra hypothesis. A grep of Mathlib finds no other definition of this isomorphism. The other matches are uses of it, plus the continuous variant `quotientEquivOfIsTopCompl` in Topology/Algebra/Module/Complement.lean, which is built from it. So the definition is faithful and not too narrow.
